title: Made-to-measure cutting boards
description: A solid wood cutting board made for your worktop: dimensions, wood, stop edge and details agreed personally with Edle Hölzer.
intro: Your worktop. Your dimensions. We make solid wood boards around the way you cook, the space available and the character of your kitchen.
imageAlt: A completed large oak cutting board with a stop edge

sections.title: Made for real kitchens
sections.text: Our completed projects are starting points, not a fixed catalogue of sizes. Oak and Yellow Poplar show how different woods can change the appearance of a substantial board. We choose suitable timber together, based on use, budget and availability.
sections.more: A custom board does not have to be XXL. We can also discuss a smaller serving board, matching breakfast boards for your family or a holder made for a board you already own. Tell us what you want to use it for before deciding on the details.

sections.title: Dimensions, material and handling
sections.text: Measure the usable worktop, including the space you need around the board. Consider the sink, hob, cupboards and where you will lift or store it. Thickness, construction and wood affect the weight as well as the appearance.
sections.more: We discuss edge grain or end grain, rounded or bevelled edges, grip recesses, a stop edge and a juice groove where suitable. Engraving needs a position that works with the design and leaves the working area practical. Not every combination is sensible; we will say so openly.

sections.title: A realistic price framework
sections.text: Depending on size and specification, custom pieces can start at a few hundred euros. We calculate your board individually; there is no universal price per centimetre.
sections.more: Our 75 × 60 cm XXL reference board with a stop edge starts at €1,199 and can reach around €1,600–1,700 depending on specification. This is an upper-range example, not a minimum budget or the quoted price of the photographed customer projects.

sections.title: From first idea to your finished board
sections.text: Send your intended use and any rough dimensions. We discuss feasibility, wood, a price range and production time. We make the agreed design only after your approval.
sections.more: A kitchen photo can help, but you do not need one for the first enquiry. If you are unsure about wood or construction, leave those choices open. We agree collection or dispatch as part of the project; a custom build does not automatically have the dispatch time of a ready-made product.

faq: Can I order any size?
We check whether the proposed dimensions, thickness and construction are suitable. Available timber, stability, weight and everyday handling all matter.
Can you add a juice groove or engraving?
Yes, where the board and intended use allow it. We agree the position and design before production.
Does an enquiry place an order?
No. We first discuss your idea, feasibility, budget and timing. Production requires your approval.

title: Wooden spatulas
description: Handcrafted solid wood spatulas with a personal choice of grain, optional engraving and care advice from Edle Hölzer.
intro: A simple kitchen tool with its own grain and feel. Our solid wood spatulas are made for turning, moving and serving food in everyday cooking.
imageAlt: A solid wood spatula used in a frying pan

sections.title: Choose the wood and your favourite piece
sections.text: Depending on the current selection, we make spatulas from oak, walnut, ash, beech, chestnut, Kambala or Wenge. The orderable woods and edge shapes are shown in the Etsy listing.
sections.more: If several pieces of your chosen wood are available, we can send photos so you can choose your favourite grain. Optional engraving is discussed individually, with a mock-up before it is made.

sections.title: A considered tool for your pan
sections.text: A wooden spatula works without a metal edge against the pan. Smoothly finished surfaces and a length of around 30 cm give it a comfortable feel and keep your hand away from the hot pan.
sections.more: Use it without unnecessary pressure, including on coated pans. Check edges regularly for rough spots. Wood is a solid material, not a flexible plastic blade, and should not be used as a lever.

sections.title: Clean briefly. Let it dry freely.
sections.text: Wash by hand after cooking, wipe dry and allow air to circulate around the tool. Do not put it in the dishwasher or leave it soaking.
sections.more: If the surface begins to feel dry or rough, suitable wood care can refresh it. Our care guide explains cleaning, drying and applying a thin coat without leaving excess on the surface.

sections.title: Build a small, useful kitchen collection
sections.text: Pair a spatula with a wooden dough scraper or butter knife in a complementary wood. Start with tools you will actually use rather than collecting unnecessary accessories.

faq: Can I choose an individual spatula?
If more than one example of a wood is available, ask us for photos before dispatch.
Is it dishwasher safe?
No. Brief hand washing, drying with a cloth and free air drying are the appropriate routine.
Are all woods always available?
No. Check the current Etsy listing for the woods and versions available to order.

title: Cutting boards with engraving
description: Personal engraving on a handcrafted wooden cutting board: choose a clear motif and agree the position with Edle Hölzer before production.
intro: A name, a date or a clear motif can turn a useful board into a personal gift. We help you find a position that belongs on the board, not in the way of using it.
imageAlt: A wooden cutting board with a personal engraving along the edge
cta: Find a board for my engraving

sections.title: Keep the message clear
sections.text: Short names, dates, lettering and simple motifs usually work best. Light wood often makes an engraving more visible than dark or strongly figured timber.
sections.more: Tell us the occasion and the result you have in mind. For business logos, the clarity of the artwork and the available space matter more than the number of details. We check whether a motif is suitable instead of promising that every file will work.

sections.title: Choose the position together
sections.text: An edge, corner, handle area, underside or dedicated serving area may suit the design. The right position depends on the board and its intended use.
sections.more: An engraving in a frequently used cutting area will be exposed to knife marks. A juice groove and engraving also need space to coexist. We discuss these details and provide a mock-up before making the engraving.

sections.title: A personal detail, not a separate product
sections.text: Choose your board first, then agree the engraving. Cutting-board engraving costs €10; the available options are shown on the relevant product page.
sections.more: For dough scrapers, spatulas and butter knives, send your text or artwork and discuss it with us. The product photos show examples; they are not a promise that every layout suits every piece.

sections.title: From idea to approval
sections.text: Send your chosen product and wording or motif. We discuss legibility and placement, prepare the mock-up and make the engraving after you approve it.

faq: Can every board be engraved?
In principle we can engrave wooden boards, but we check the material, available space, motif and intended use first.
Can you engrave a company logo?
Yes, if the artwork and scale are suitable. We discuss the layout before making it.
Is a bigger engraving better?
Not necessarily. A clear, well-positioned engraving often fits a board better than a large design in the working area.

title: Quality wooden kitchen accessories
description: Solid wood boards, spatulas, dough scrapers and care products: a small, useful kitchen collection made by Edle Hölzer in Central Hesse.
intro: Fewer accessories. More substance. A good kitchen collection starts with useful tools, a pleasant feel and materials you enjoy using every day.
imageAlt: A wooden spatula in use while cooking

sections.title: Start with what you use daily
sections.text: A substantial cutting board provides a working surface. A smaller snack board serves breakfast or an evening meal. A spatula turns food, while a dough scraper gathers chopped ingredients or handles dough.
sections.more: Choose a juice groove if you regularly work with juicy food and the board is suitable. It is an option with a purpose, not a detail every board needs. Size, weight and available storage should guide your choice.

sections.title: Quality is more than the name of the wood
sections.text: Look at the surface, edges, joints and handling. A tool should feel comfortable, have a suitable construction and fit the work it is meant to do.
sections.more: Colour and grain make each piece individual, but they do not replace careful workmanship. We select timber and check the finished pieces in our workshop. If you are unsure, we can help you compare suitable products.

sections.title: Care belongs to the collection
sections.text: Wash wooden tools by hand, wipe them dry and let air circulate around them. Appropriate care refreshes a dry surface and supports long-term use.
sections.more: Our care balm combines linseed-oil varnish and regional beeswax. Check the individual product page for its price and what is included; not every board or accessory automatically includes a tin.

sections.title: A gift that has a place in the kitchen
sections.text: Choose a familiar daily ritual rather than an anonymous decorative object. A board, dough scraper or spatula can be personalised with an individually agreed engraving.

faq: Which accessories are useful?
Start with your cooking habits: a suitable board and one or two tools you will regularly use.
Do wooden tools need complicated care?
No. Hand washing, drying and occasional suitable surface care are the essentials. Avoid the dishwasher and prolonged soaking.
Can I combine matching woods?
Yes, subject to the current selection. We can help you choose complementary pieces.

title: Walnut cutting boards
description: Choose a walnut cutting board by grain, construction, weight and intended use, with personal advice from the Edle Hölzer workshop.
intro: Dark heartwood, individual grain and a warm feel. Walnut is a considered choice for a board that remains visible in the kitchen and is used every day.
imageAlt: Walnut cutting boards with different colours and grain patterns

sections.title: Choose more than a colour
sections.text: Grain, surface, weight and size all influence how a walnut board feels in everyday use. A compact board that is easy to lift serves a different purpose from a heavy board that stays on the worktop.
sections.more: For our pure walnut boards, we select the darker heartwood. Natural differences in colour and grain remain part of the material. A photograph represents an individual piece, not a uniform industrial colour.

sections.title: Working board or serving board?
sections.text: Both are possible, but the useful format may differ. Cutting needs enough clear working area; serving also depends on what you will carry, arrange and place on the table.
sections.more: Think about where the board will live and whether you need to move it often. A dark walnut surface creates contrast on a light worktop and can sit quietly alongside darker cabinetry. Judge the whole piece, not only the wood species.

sections.title: Walnut or oak?
sections.text: In our experience, oak is more resistant to visible use marks than walnut. Walnut is softer, so its surface can show use sooner. Both can be good everyday boards.
sections.more: Do not decide on hardness alone. Your knives, preferred feel, kitchen design, the board's weight and your care routine also matter. We help you compare actual pieces rather than treating a hardness number as a complete buying guide.

sections.title: End grain or edge grain?
sections.text: Construction changes the visible grain and the character of the working surface. Compare the available formats and their weight as well as their appearance.
sections.more: A larger end-grain block may suit a permanent preparation area. A smaller edge-grain board can be easier to lift and put away. Neither description alone tells you whether a board fits your kitchen.

sections.title: Care with a light hand
sections.text: Clean briefly by hand, dry with a cloth and let both sides release moisture. Apply suitable care thinly and remove excess rather than leaving a glossy layer.
sections.more: Wood moves as moisture changes. Avoid prolonged soaking, dishwashers and drying against strong heat. If a board needs more than routine care, ask us whether refurbishment is appropriate for its condition.

faq: Is walnut suitable for daily cutting?
Yes, when construction, dimensions and care suit the intended use. Expect natural signs of use rather than an untouched decorative surface.
Is walnut harder than oak?
No. In our workshop experience, oak is more resistant to visible marks. The choice should also consider feel, weight and appearance.
Why do walnut boards look different?
Natural colour and grain vary between pieces. Wood selection and construction also affect the finished appearance.

title: BBQ gifts and Pitmaster Boards
description: A solid wood Pitmaster Board for carving, resting and serving: choose a useful BBQ gift with personal advice from Edle Hölzer.
intro: Made for the moment after the grill. A solid wood Pitmaster Board gives carving, arranging and serving a proper place at the table.
imageAlt: Steak served on a wooden board as a BBQ gift

sections.title: Choose for the food and the cook
sections.text: A steak lover, smoker owner and host preparing food for a group do not necessarily need the same board. Match the working area to the food and leave enough room for carving and serving.
sections.more: Large cuts can benefit from a substantial surface, but a board that is difficult to carry or wash may be the wrong gift. Consider worktop space, weight, grip and where it will be stored.

sections.title: What makes a useful Pitmaster Board?
sections.text: A stable working surface, appropriate dimensions and comfortable handling matter more than decorative extras. A juice groove can help with juicy food where the board is suitable.
sections.more: We discuss a surrounding groove or an additional collecting basin when appropriate. A large format alone does not make a board better; construction, thickness and the way it is used need to work together.

sections.title: A personal detail for a real occasion
sections.text: A name, date or restrained motif can make a BBQ board a personal birthday, wedding or housewarming gift. We agree the engraving position before it is made.
sections.more: Keep the main cutting area usable and allow space for any groove. If a standard format does not suit the recipient's grill station or kitchen island, we can discuss a made-to-measure board.

sections.title: A gift made to be used
sections.text: Wood will show use. A thoughtful gift includes an understanding of cleaning, drying and care, rather than an expectation that the board must remain untouched.

faq: What size should a BBQ board be?
Choose around the food, available worktop, handling and cleaning space. We can advise on a suitable existing or custom format.
Can it be engraved?
Yes, subject to the board and motif. We agree a position that works with the working area and any juice groove.
Does every BBQ board need a juice groove?
No. It depends on the food and intended use. We recommend it only where it makes sense for the board.

title: Thoughtful gifts made from wood
description: Handcrafted wooden gifts for daily rituals: cutting boards, kitchen tools and personal engraving from Edle Hölzer in Central Hesse.
intro: A gift becomes personal when it belongs to someone's everyday life. Start with the person, the occasion and the way the piece will be used.
imageAlt: A wooden cutting board presented with care balm and a care guide

sections.title: Choose a ritual, not just an object
sections.text: Breakfast, baking, preparing dinner and sharing food each suggest different pieces. A butter knife or dough scraper can be as thoughtful as a large board if it fits the recipient.
sections.more: Consider space, weight and how often the piece will be used. A serving board suits a different routine from a permanently placed chopping block. We can help you choose within your budget.

sections.title: A shared design for the family
sections.text: Matching breakfast boards or complementary kitchen tools can connect individual gifts without making every piece identical. Natural grain still gives each one its own character.
sections.more: We discuss wood, format and personal details together. Availability can vary, so a photo selection is useful where several individual pieces are in stock.

sections.title: Personalise with care
sections.text: An individually agreed engraving can add a name, date or short message. We prepare a mock-up before making it and choose a position that suits the product.
sections.more: For company gifts, quantity, budget per piece and timing are important from the start. Our dedicated corporate page provides an enquiry route for that discussion.

sections.title: Know what comes with the gift
sections.text: The specific product page lists the contents. Extra pieces or care products shown in a photograph are not automatically included with every product.
sections.more: Tell us if you would like to combine items. We agree the actual pieces and presentation rather than treating a sample photograph as a universal set.

faq: Can a wooden gift be personalised?
Yes, where the piece and motif are suitable. We agree the engraving with you before production.
Do you offer gifts for businesses?
Yes. Tell us the quantity, budget and occasion through our corporate gifts page.
How should the recipient care for it?
Hand wash, dry and allow air to circulate. Follow the care guidance for the specific product.

title: Press and people behind Edle Hölzer
description: Meet Özgür and Serkan Koç and the Edle Hölzer workshop in Central Hesse. Background, craft, materials and contact for press enquiries.
intro: Edle Hölzer is a small woodcraft workshop in Central Hesse. We make boards and kitchen tools with individual grain, direct personal advice and a focus on keeping good pieces in use.
imageAlt: Özgür working at the table saw in the Edle Hölzer workshop

sections.title: Özgür: design, timber and craftsmanship
sections.text: Özgür Koç founded Edle Hölzer and has worked in skilled crafts for around 20 years. He is responsible for design, wood selection and production.
sections.more: The boards are traditionally worked by hand, deliberately without CNC. The material, intended use, edges, surface and handling are considered together rather than judged by wood species alone.

sections.title: Serkan: making the details visible
sections.text: Serkan Koç is an engineer and amateur photographer, responsible for the online presence. Through photography and video he brings the craft, materials and details of the work into view.

sections.title: Stories from the workshop
sections.text: Care instead of disposal, choosing material for a purpose and working with historic timber are recurring themes. The numbered Erbstück series gives selected old wood another role.
sections.more: Not every old beam is suitable for a cutting board. We assess the substance, cracks and grain before deciding whether to make a piece. Existing traces can remain part of its character; suitability comes first.

sections.title: A digital space for personal advice
sections.text: The website helps people compare formats, learn about care and consider a board in their own kitchen. Custom projects begin with a conversation about use, dimensions and budget.
sections.more: For press, collaborations, workshop photography or questions about a specific piece, please contact us. Image use and publication rights must be agreed; photographs on the website are not a blanket licence to reuse them.

title: Solid wood cutting boards
description: Choose a solid wood cutting board by use, construction, weight and material, with personal advice from Edle Hölzer in Central Hesse.
intro: A useful board starts with the way you cook. Choose a format you can comfortably use, clean and store, then consider the wood and the details.
imageAlt: An oak end-grain cutting board with shaped grips and visible growth rings

sections.title: What solid wood means
sections.text: The working surface is made from real wood rather than a thin decorative veneer. A board may be made from a single piece or carefully joined elements. Edge-grain and end-grain constructions show the material in different ways.
sections.more: Sufficient material can allow future sanding and refurbishment where the condition is suitable. Solid wood is not indestructible: moisture, heat, cracks and failed joints still need appropriate assessment.

sections.title: Match the format to everyday use
sections.text: For daily preparation, leave enough clear working space. A breakfast or snack board can be smaller and easier to carry. A substantial chopping block is better suited to remaining on the worktop.
sections.more: A juice groove, grip recesses, engraving or a custom format each serve a different purpose. Choose useful details rather than assuming the largest or most heavily equipped board is the best one.

sections.title: Care and repair
sections.text: Wash briefly by hand, wipe dry and let both sides release moisture. Do not use the dishwasher or leave the board soaking. Refresh a dry surface with suitable care.
sections.more: For a rough or deeply scratched board, ask whether sanding or workshop refurbishment is appropriate. Surface care does not repair a structural crack or an opening joint.

faq: Is solid wood always one single piece?
No. Joined solid wood elements are also solid wood. The construction and workmanship matter.
What thickness should I choose?
Consider size, weight and handling together. A thicker board can offer substance but is also heavier.
Where can I check delivery and availability?
The individual product page links to the current Etsy offer, where the orderable version and conditions are shown.

title: Solid oak cutting boards
description: Oak cutting boards for preparation, serving and BBQ: choose the construction, dimensions and weight that fit your kitchen.
intro: A visible grain, a substantial feel and an individual surface. Oak is a practical everyday choice when the actual board fits your kitchen and routine.
imageAlt: A substantial oak end-grain cutting board with shaped edges and grips

sections.title: Oak in everyday use
sections.text: In our workshop experience, oak is more resistant to visible use marks than walnut. It can be a good choice if durability of the surface matters to you. Colour, grain and weight should still be part of the decision.
sections.more: The open-looking grain is part of the wood's character. Judge the finished surface and workmanship rather than the appearance of pores alone. Natural colour changes and patina can develop with use.

sections.title: Edge grain or end grain?
sections.text: Edge grain shows the lengthwise grain; end grain shows the ends of the fibres. Both can make useful boards. Compare the actual dimensions, thickness and handling rather than choosing by the construction name alone.
sections.more: A board for breakfast or serving may need to be easy to carry. A large preparation or BBQ board may remain on the worktop. Choose a juice groove where it suits the food and board, not simply as decoration.

sections.title: Surface changes need context
sections.text: Dark marks on oak are not automatically mould. Oak's tannins can react with iron and moisture. If you are unsure about a mark, ask us before deciding how to treat it.
sections.more: Do not treat every dark patch as the same issue. Condition, smell, moisture exposure and the actual surface need to be assessed. Keep the board clean and let it dry freely instead of leaving it damp against the worktop.

sections.title: Made to keep using
sections.text: Suitable oak boards can be refreshed or refurbished when their condition allows it. Care and careful drying support long-term use, but do not make wood immune to damage.

faq: Is oak suitable for cutting boards?
Yes, with suitable construction, finishing and care. Choose a particular board that fits your use.
Is oak better than walnut?
Neither is universally better. Oak is more resistant to visible marks in our experience; feel, appearance and weight also matter.
Can an oak board be refurbished?
Often, where the substance and condition are suitable. We assess it before recommending a service.

title: Oak or walnut cutting board?
description: Compare oak and walnut by appearance, everyday handling, use marks and care, with advice based on Edle Hölzer's workshop experience.
intro: Start with your kitchen and how you use a board, not a ranking of wood species. Both oak and walnut can be good everyday companions.
imageAlt: A light oak cutting board with visible natural grain

sections.title: Oak: structure and resistance to visible marks
sections.text: Oak has a visible grain and often creates a lighter impression. In our experience it is more resistant to visible use marks than walnut. It still needs cleaning, drying and occasional surface care.
sections.more: The actual piece of timber matters: colour, growth rings, knots and construction all change the result. Do not assume every oak board will look or feel the same.

sections.title: Walnut: warm colour and a different feel
sections.text: Walnut's darker heartwood can create contrast in a light kitchen or a quieter transition alongside dark cabinets. It is softer than oak and can show use sooner.
sections.more: Hardness alone is not a complete guide to knife friendliness or daily comfort. Consider your knives, preferred feel, construction and care, as well as the board's weight.

sections.title: Compare the boards, not just the woods
sections.text: Two boards of different sizes or constructions are not a like-for-like comparison. Check dimensions, thickness, weight and how easily you can lift, wash and store each one.
sections.more: For serving, the presentation and handling may lead the choice. For daily preparation, the clear working area can matter more. We can help you compare available pieces and their grain before you decide.

faq: Which wood suits a light kitchen?
Walnut can add contrast, while oak can continue a lighter palette. The actual worktop and grain matter.
Can oak develop dark marks?
Yes. Tannins can react with iron and moisture. A dark mark is not automatically mould; ask if you are unsure.
Is walnut always more expensive?
Compare actual boards. Size, construction, wood selection and details all influence price.

title: Solid wood end-grain cutting boards
description: Understand end-grain cutting boards: construction, weight, joints and care, with handcrafted examples from Edle Hölzer.
intro: The ends of the wood fibres form the working surface. This construction creates distinctive patterns, but the pattern alone is not proof of quality.
imageAlt: An end-grain cutting board with a distinctive solid wood pattern

sections.title: What end grain means
sections.text: Pieces are arranged so that the ends of their fibres face upwards. The arrangement creates the visible pattern and the character of the working surface.
sections.more: End grain is not automatically better than edge grain. Workmanship, suitable timber and the way the board is used are equally important. Choose for your cooking routine rather than a pattern alone.

sections.title: Substance has weight
sections.text: A large end-grain board can be substantial and heavy. That may suit a permanent preparation area, but makes lifting, cleaning and putting it away a different task.
sections.more: Before choosing, measure the working area and consider how you will carry and wash the board. A lighter or smaller format may be more practical if it needs to move often.

sections.title: Look at joints and the whole surface
sections.text: Check the finish, edges, flatness and joints. A crack or opening joint is different from an ordinary knife mark and should be assessed rather than covered with more oil.
sections.more: Wood responds to changing moisture. Cleaning and allowing both sides to dry are important. Suitable care supports the surface, but does not repair structural damage.

faq: Is end grain always better?
No. Compare workmanship, dimensions, handling and intended use as well as construction.
Can an end-grain board crack?
Wood can move and develop damage, especially with unsuitable moisture exposure. Ask for an assessment of cracks or opening joints.
How should I care for it?
Hand wash briefly, wipe dry and let both sides dry freely. Follow the care guide and apply suitable care thinly.

title: Thoughtful wooden gifts for men
description: Choose a useful wooden gift for the man you are buying for: cooking, BBQ, serving and personal engraving from Edle Hölzer.
intro: Choose around his daily rituals, not a generic gift category. Cooking, sharing food or working at the grill can each suggest a different wooden piece.
imageAlt: Steak arranged on a wooden serving board

sections.title: For the way he cooks
sections.text: A regular home cook may appreciate a practical preparation board. For someone who enjoys BBQ, consider carving and serving space. A host may prefer a piece that moves easily from kitchen to table.
sections.more: Consider the recipient's worktop, storage and ability to lift the board. Bigger is not automatically more thoughtful. A smaller tool that is used often can be the better gift.

sections.title: Make it personal without overloading it
sections.text: A name, date or short message can be engraved where the product is suitable. We agree the design and position with you and prepare a mock-up before making it.
sections.more: Leave room for the working area and any juice groove. If several individual pieces of a wood are available, ask us about choosing a favourite grain.

sections.title: A gift that stays useful
sections.text: A wooden piece should fit a real routine, whether the occasion is a birthday, housewarming, wedding or Christmas. Check the product's contents, availability and delivery information before ordering.

faq: What makes a good wooden gift?
A piece suited to the recipient's habits, space and preferred feel, rather than size or decoration alone.
Can the gift be engraved?
Yes, where the piece and motif are suitable. The layout is agreed before production.
Is a board a suitable BBQ gift?
It can be, if its working area, weight and handling suit the way the recipient grills and serves.

title: Thoughtful wooden gifts for women
description: Personal wooden gifts for cooking, baking and sharing food: choose a useful individual piece from the Edle Hölzer workshop.
intro: A thoughtful gift reflects the person receiving it. Start with what she enjoys doing, the space she uses and the small rituals that matter to her.
imageAlt: A wooden kitchen tool being used while cooking

sections.title: Choose for a real daily ritual
sections.text: For someone who bakes, a wooden dough scraper can be a useful companion. A breakfast board or butter knife suits a different routine. Cooking and sharing food may suggest a preparation or serving board.
sections.more: Use those habits as starting points, not assumptions. The format, weight, grain and storage space should fit the person and her kitchen.

sections.title: A personal choice of wood and detail
sections.text: Wood varies naturally in colour and grain. If several examples are available, we can help choose a favourite piece. A restrained engraving adds a personal detail where suitable.
sections.more: We discuss the text, motif and position and prepare a mock-up before making the engraving. A clear, well-placed detail usually works better than a design that takes over the working area.

sections.title: Something to keep using
sections.text: A birthday, wedding, housewarming or Christmas gift can become part of daily life rather than remaining decoration. Read the individual product page for the actual contents, availability and care guidance.

faq: Which wood should I choose?
Look at the actual grain and colour alongside the recipient's preferred feel and kitchen. We can help compare suitable pieces.
Is personalisation possible?
Yes, with an individually agreed engraving where the product and motif are suitable.
Does the photographed set always come together?
No. Check the specific product page for what is included and ask us if you want to combine items.

title: Cutting boards from our German workshop
description: How Edle Hölzer makes solid wood cutting boards in Central Hesse: timber selection, construction, finishing and individual checks before dispatch.
intro: From selecting timber to packing the finished piece, we take responsibility for the work in our workshop in Central Hesse. The process matters as much as the name of the wood.
imageAlt: Wood being cut at the table saw in the Edle Hölzer workshop

sections.title: From timber to a considered construction
sections.text: We source wood, record the stock, inventory and store it, and allow controlled drying. We then select and cut suitable pieces and determine the construction for the intended board.
sections.more: Material, machine work and handwork belong together. We discuss a particular wood's source where relevant rather than presenting every piece as having the same regional origin.

sections.title: Shape, surface and finish
sections.text: We work the faces, shape and functional details, then sand and finish the board. The edge, grip and feel are considered together. Our boards are traditionally made by hand, deliberately without CNC.
sections.more: The wood species alone does not prove quality. Construction, workmanship and the finished piece need to be judged together. We explain material choices and the origin of the wood as specifically as we can.

sections.title: Before a board leaves the workshop
sections.text: We check the finished piece, photograph it naturally, then pack and dispatch it. Each board receives another close look before shipping.
sections.more: Our preparation includes a fresh fine sanding where appropriate, linseed-oil finish and our care balm. The care guide explains our process and the difference between workshop preparation and routine care at home.

sections.title: A workshop relationship beyond the purchase
sections.text: Custom boards begin with a discussion about the kitchen and intended use. Existing boards may be suitable for refurbishment, subject to their condition. We can help you decide which next step makes sense.

faq: Where do you make the boards?
In our workshop in Central Hesse, Germany.
Is all the wood from the same region?
No. We discuss the source and availability of the wood for the actual product rather than making one blanket origin claim.
Is all wood FSC certified?
We do not claim that every piece is FSC certified. Ask about the specific material and available evidence.
Can a used board be refurbished?
Where the substance and condition are suitable, we can assess it for refurbishment. The service is currently offered within Germany.

title: Privacy notice
description: Information about data processing, hosting, consent, contact forms, optional analytics and your rights on the Edle Hölzer website.
intro: English translation of our German privacy notice. This notice describes the technical setup of the website and does not replace a legal review of the applicable legal bases and wording.

sections.title: 1. Controller
sections.text: Edle Hölzer GbR, Özgür Koç and Serkan Koç, Schulgasse 4A, 35460 Staufenberg, Germany. Email: info@edlehoelzer.de.

sections.title: 2. Access data and server logs
sections.text: When you access this website, the hosting provider automatically records your IP address, date and time, browser type and version, operating system, referring URL and the pages or files requested. These data are technically necessary to provide the website and ensure its stability and security. The legal basis is Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. The data are deleted when they are no longer required.

sections.title: 3. Hosting
sections.text: This website is provided through GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. Technically necessary personal data, particularly server logs, are processed when you visit. Processing serves the provision and secure delivery of this website under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Processing on servers in the USA cannot be ruled out. Further information is available in GitHub's privacy statement, linked below.

sections.title: Consent management and optional services
sections.text: On your first visit, you can decide whether statistics services and external media may be loaded in addition to technically necessary functions. Your choice is stored locally in your browser so that you do not have to choose again on every page. Without your consent, we do not load statistics, marketing or external-media scripts. You can change your choice at any time using Cookie settings in the footer.

sections.title: Web analytics with Umami and GoatCounter
sections.text: If you consent to Statistics, we use Umami and GoatCounter for data-minimising audience and intent measurement. This includes page views, referrers, device types and selected interactions such as product views, Etsy clicks, comparisons and contact actions. We do not collect free-text form entries or message contents. Product-related events are technically reduced so that freely entered content is not transmitted. Processing takes place only with your consent, under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and, where access to information on your device is involved, the relevant TDDDG provision. Providers: Umami Software, Inc. and GoatCounter. Their privacy notices are linked below.

sections.title: 4. Contact by email
sections.text: If you contact us by email, we process the information you provide to handle your enquiry. The legal bases are Article 6(1)(b) GDPR for pre-contractual steps and Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. The data are deleted once the enquiry has been completed and no statutory retention obligations remain.

sections.title: 5. Contact form: Formspree
sections.text: If you contact us through a form on this website, the information entered, such as name, company, email address, telephone number, message and further voluntary details, is transmitted to and processed by Formspree Inc., USA. Processing serves the handling of your enquiry under Article 6(1)(b) and Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Data may be processed on servers outside the European Union, particularly in the USA. Formspree states that it uses appropriate safeguards to protect personal data. Its privacy policy is linked below.

sections.title: 6. External links: Etsy
sections.text: This website contains links to our Etsy shop. Clicking a link takes you away from our website. Etsy is solely responsible for data processing on Etsy.

sections.title: Pinterest Developer App and Pinterest API
sections.text: Edle Hölzer may use a Pinterest Developer App or the Pinterest API to manage its own content, product information, pins, boards and analytics more efficiently, including planning, publishing, management and analysis. Depending on use and technical implementation, processing may include Pinterest account IDs or profile information, board and pin information, published content and metadata, API permissions or scopes, OAuth access tokens and, where applicable, refresh tokens, plus technical logs for troubleshooting and security.
sections.more: OAuth tokens are stored and used only for the specified purposes where necessary to technically provide, automate, manage and analyse Edle Hölzer's own Pinterest activities. They must not appear publicly in frontend code, the repository or client code; they must be stored server-side or in secure secret management. The legal basis is our legitimate interest under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR unless consent or another legal basis applies. Pinterest's privacy policy, terms of service and developer terms also apply; links are provided below.

sections.title: External media
sections.text: Some pages may contain embedded videos. These media are loaded only after you consent to the relevant category. Before that, only a local placeholder is displayed. The provider of the currently embedded videos is Google Ireland Limited through YouTube or YouTube-nocookie. Loading a video may transmit personal data to Google.

sections.title: Google Preferred Sources
sections.text: Editorial pages offer a button to select Edle Hölzer as a preferred source on Google. The Google library needed for this feature is not loaded when you open the page. Only when you deliberately activate the button is a connection to Google established and the selection dialogue opened. Your IP address and browser and device data may then be transmitted to Google. By clicking, you expressly request this external function. The provider is Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland. Google's privacy policy is linked below.

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.text: You have the right to access under Article 15 GDPR, rectification under Article 16, erasure under Article 17, restriction of processing under Article 18, data portability under Article 20 where applicable, and objection under Article 21. You can contact us by email at any time. You also have the right to complain to a data protection authority.
